target_audience: First-year university calculus students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The 'Hidden' Variable: Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Introduce the difference between explicit functions (y=f(x)) and implicit relations. Use a visual comparison: a straight line (easy to see y) versus a circle (where x and y are tangled). Explain that we still need to find the slope (dy/dx) even when y isn't isolated.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic drone flying in a perfect circle defined by x² + y² = 25. Ask: 'How do we find its vertical speed relative to its horizontal position at any point?'

sections.title: Prerequisite Tool: The Chain Rule Review
sections.content: Briefly refresh the Chain Rule, focusing on the derivative of a function inside another function. Use a 'nested gear' animation where turning the 'x' gear moves the 'y' gear, which then moves the 'result' gear. Emphasize that d/dx[yⁿ] = n·yⁿ⁻¹ · (dy/dx).
sections.example: Differentiating [f(x)]³ becomes 3[f(x)]² · f'(x). Similarly, d/dx[y³] becomes 3y² · (dy/dx).

sections.title: The Four-Step Process
sections.content: Break down the algorithm into four visual steps: 1. Differentiate both sides with respect to x. 2. Apply the Chain Rule to every 'y' term (tagging them with dy/dx). 3. Group all terms containing dy/dx on one side. 4. Factor out and solve for dy/dx.
sections.example: Equation: x² + y² = 25. Step 1: d/dx(x²) + d/dx(y²) = d/dx(25). Step 2: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Step 3: 2y(dy/dx) = -2x. Step 4: dy/dx = -x/y.

sections.title: Graphical Interpretation & Verification
sections.content: Show a graph of the circle x² + y² = 25 with a dynamic tangent line. Move a point (x, y) around the circle and show how the formula dy/dx = -x/y perfectly matches the slope of the visual tangent line at any coordinate.
sections.example: At point (3, 4) on the circle, the slope dy/dx = -3/4. Show an animation of a character 'Slopey the Snail' sliding down this exact 0.75-grade incline.

sections.title: Complex Application: The Folium of Descartes
sections.content: Apply the technique to a more complex 'loop' curve (x³ + y³ = 6xy). This demonstrates the power of implicit differentiation over trying to solve for 'y' algebraically, which would be nearly impossible.
sections.example: A specialized 'magnetic track' for a toy car shaped like a loop-de-loop. Use the product rule on the '6xy' term: d/dx(6xy) = 6y + 6x(dy/dx). This highlights the integration of multiple derivative rules.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
sections.content: Recap the essential 'Golden Rule': Whenever you differentiate a term with 'y', you MUST multiply by dy/dx. Remind students that dy/dx is simply the rate of change, regardless of how messy the equation looks.
sections.example: A final visual checklist: 'Did you use Chain Rule on y?' 'Did you isolate dy/dx?' 'Does the result represent a slope?'
